title: Route mapping regression caused tier misassignment across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A routing regression introduced in the route-mapping cache layer caused requests to be assigned to the wrong capacity tier (dedicated vs shared) and, in some cases, to the wrong region. This affected a small set of customers using Reserved/Dedicated pools and Private VPC endpoints and led to increased latency, quota violations, and billing discrepancies. Impact window: 2026-03-09 02:30Z to 2026-03-10 07:10Z.

Scope: Hosted API customers experienced incorrect fallbacks from dedicated to shared models; Dedicated customers observed unexpected routing to lower-priority racks causing higher queuing latency; Private customers with strict region pins received cross-region routing for a subset of requests. The issue manifested under burst load combined with cache churn after a deployment to the routing service.

Root cause hypothesis: A recent refactor of the route mapping cache invalidation (PR gh.com/redwood-inference/routing#4123) changed the ordering of evaluation of policies: tier-priority ordering and region affinity checks were evaluated after a compatibility fallback step. Under cache misses, the compatibility fallback returned an available-but-incompatible variant before the tier and region filters ran, causing misassignment. Edge conditions with concurrent cache refreshes could surface stale policy blobs.

Reproduction steps: 1) Use the repro harness at gh.com/redwood-inference/routing/tree/repro/ENG-17283. 2) Create a tenant with a Dedicated pool and strict region pin. 3) Generate burst traffic that triggers cache churn (see payloads/loadtests/dedicated-burst.json). 4) Observe routing logs via /routes/debug and see decisions where compatibility matched before tier/region checks.

Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Rolled back routing service to tag routing-v1.67 (2026-03-09 03:12Z) to stop ongoing misroutes. 2) Enabled a hotfix policy that forces region-affinity checks prior to compatibility fallback for impacted tenants. 3) Contacted customers in the incident group with post-rollback summary and temporary credits where billing was affected.

Proposed permanent fix: 1) Rework evaluation order in the route evaluation pipeline so that tier and region predicates are applied before any compatibility fallback. 2) Harden cache invalidation with versioned policy blobs and atomic swap to avoid partial reads during refresh. 3) Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent cache refreshes and verify ordering invariants. 4) Add end-to-end smoke tests for Dedicated and Private tenant flows in CI with synthetic burst scenarios.

Acceptance criteria: 1) No regression in route decision order across a 24-hour soak test under synthetic bursts. 2) Unit tests covering evaluation order added and green. 3) Benchmarked latency and routing correctness results committed to the runbook. 4) Customer-facing incident postmortem published and affected customers confirmed no residual impact.

Notes: This ticket spans Hosted, Dedicated and Private code paths in the routing layer. The fix must be backward-compatible with older policy schemas and can’t introduce additional latency in the common fast-path. Consider feature-flagging the stricter evaluation for a rollout window and use canary tenants to validate behavior before global enablement.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision tenant with Dedicated pool and strict region pin
Run dedicated-burst.json load script from repro harness
Watch /routes/debug and routing decision logs for tier and region mismatch entries
